assets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Refine image 1, the current APFELWURM title art, toward image 2's softer and more detailed storybook look. Use image 2 only as the STYLE reference: a soft, richly painted storybook game illustration with subtle natural texture on grass, bark and apple, believable warm daylight, rounded softly modeled forms and gentle depth. A little realism is welcome, while the worm remains cute and approachable. Keep the worm entirely warm tangerine/apricot ORANGE with golden highlights and gentle brown shading, cheerful blue eyes and a tiny closed smile. No pink or red worm, teeth or creepy face. Preserve the red apple. Preserve image 1's full landscape 3:2 composition, exact APFELWURM logo/spelling, orange worm with curved segmented body next to the apple, sunny garden and path into the forest, and quiet lower area for the REAL Play button. More subtle shading and organic surfaces, fewer hard flat outlines, beautiful polished game illustration. Deliver the illustration alone. Do not copy the app window frame, title bar, cursor, screenshot borders or Play button from image 2. No extra text, interface, watermark or black border.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: final mobile game title artwork, tall portrait 1:2 aspect ratio, 1024 by 2048 pixels (or a taller 9:20 canvas). Use the referenced APFELWURM picture only as the character and detailed sunlit storybook style reference. Recompose the whole scene for a full-height phone: a beautiful natural apple garden leading into a leafy forest, blue sky, apple tree on left, winding path on right, soft distant hills. The same friendly golden TANGERINE ORANGE worm with big blue eyes and a small closed smile curls beside one red apple, both fully visible. Make the character and apple modest in scale, centered in the middle half of the picture so the complete body and red apple are visible on a narrow phone. The exact word APFELWURM in golden raised rounded letters with green leafy edging is smaller: about 70 percent of canvas width, safely inset at least 15 percent on either side, placed in the upper quarter with generous sky around it. Spell exactly A P F E L W U R M. Fill the ENTIRE tall image from top to bottom with the lush coherent garden illustration. Extend a softly detailed grassy foreground all the way to the very bottom for a real Play button overlay. No solid dark-green band, no fade baked into art, no empty flat area, no UI or button, no extra text. Slightly realistic natural textures and warm lighting, cute and inviting, not creepy or plastic. Preserve orange worm, red apple, complete smaller logo; no pink worm, teeth, spaceships or machines. Full bleed composition with main subjects inside the middle 70 percent width so gentle cover-cropping retains them on 9:20 and 9:16 phones.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production top-down mobile game seamless TERRAIN TEXTURE atlas, exact 4 columns by 3 rows edge-to-edge, 4:3 canvas. Use referenced atlas only for palette/style. REBUILD every texture to tile continuously: opposite edges must match in color, brightness and texture. No tile frames, beveled tile edges, shadows around each square, border strips, gutters, vertical side faces, brick-like floor checkerboard or directional gradients. Each equal square fills completely with opaque texture, directly overhead, clean softly shaded natural cartoon game art, simple restrained detail legible at 16px. Row1 left-to-right: (1) quiet near-uniform fresh meadow grass, soft very low contrast mottling, NO grass tuft; (2) the SAME meadow grass color with one tiny subtle grass mark; (3) warm compact dirt; (4) pale sand. Row2: (1) continuous dense dark green hedge canopy seen straight overhead, small broad overlapping leaves extending across all four cell edges, no outer silhouette or bottom shadow because touching tiles must form one continuous hedge wall; (2) continuous gray stone masonry wall TOP surface, seamless interlocking stones and thin mortar matching at all four edges, no outer edging; (3) calm turquoise pond water with faint small ripples and seamless edges; (4) same water shifted ripples. Row3: (1) quiet near-uniform muted moss/teal forest floor with very low contrast mottling and no clumps; (2) SAME forest floor with one tiny subtle mark; (3) continuous deep teal-green forest hedge canopy straight overhead, small broad leaves crossing all four cell edges and no perimeter shading; (4) same seamless gray stone masonry as row2cell2. The two floor variants per chapter MUST have same brightness and base color, so no checkerboard when interspersed. Hedges much darker than floors; solid water unmistakably blue. No characters, fruit, flowers, rocks on floors, text, UI, labels, outlines, padding or perspective. This is aligned texture atlas for continuous connected walls, not a screenshot or a collection of isolated raised blocks.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D top-down arcade-game SPRITE ATLAS on a truly TRANSPARENT background. Square image, EXACT 4 columns by 4 rows of equal square cells. Every sprite centered in its cell with 10% clear padding, no cell borders or labels, no background, no shadows outside the sprites. Cheerful clean 2D cartoon style with simple bold dark colored outlines, few large cel-shaded color regions, extremely legible when reduced to 16 pixels. Garden and forest worm game. STRICT row-major cell contents: Row 1: cute PINK WORM HEAD facing LEFT; same worm head facing UP; same worm head facing RIGHT; same worm head facing DOWN. Heads viewed overhead, chunky rounded shape, very large white eyes and expressive black pupils in the direction of movement. Row 2: one round pink worm BODY segment full size; same round body at three-quarter size; same round body half size for tail; one bright RED APPLE with green leaf. Row 3: one cute yellow-and-black BEE viewed overhead; one red-and-black round LADYBUG facing UP; one small friendly purple SPIDER viewed overhead; one cluster of white DAISIES with yellow centers. Row 4: one little red capped MUSHROOM; one short warm brown LOG; one grey rounded ROCK; one blue-and-yellow BUTTERFLY viewed overhead. Same pink worm throughout; no long worm bodies, each body cell is a single smooth circular segment. No text, numbers, drop shadows, realism, texture noise, green matte or grid lines. Deliver the aligned 16-sprite atlas with real alpha transparency.

Use case: stylized-concept. Two production 2D cartoon game sprites on a truly transparent background. Landscape 2:1 image split into exactly TWO equal square cells with no line or gutter: LEFT cell contains one cute small snail, warm tan round spiral shell, tiny green body and two little antennae, viewed from above; RIGHT cell contains one cute small round blue bird with a yellow beak, viewed from above. Each centered, entirely inside its own cell with 12% padding. Bold clean dark colored outline, simple large cel-shaded areas, friendly and readable at 16 pixels, matching a cheerful cartoon garden worm game. No background, ground, text, labels, shadows, realism or grid. Actual aligned sprite sheet with real alpha transparency.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this transparent 4x4 sprite atlas. Recolor ONLY the worm: make the ENTIRE worm predominantly bright tangerine/pumpkin ORANGE, including every back and body segment. Use apricot/golden-orange highlights, pale golden-orange belly and burnt-orange/brown outlines and shadows. Example main orange #F5A02A, shadow #D87916, highlight #FFD17A. Remove the tomato red/crimson coloration from the worm completely. Preserve its cute rounded shape, blue eyes, ivory eye whites, small closed friendly smile and all poses. This is a precise color adjustment, not a redesign. Apply this ONLY to the four worm heads in ROW 1 and the first THREE circular body sprites in ROW 2. Keep exact cell alignment, dimensions, shapes, directions, clear padding and alpha transparency. Keep every other sprite exactly as it is, including the red apple, bee, ladybug, spider, flowers, mushroom, log, rock and butterfly. No background, text, labels or grid.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this transparent 4x4 cartoon game sprite atlas. Change ONLY the four ORANGE WORM HEADS in the FIRST ROW. Make each a much larger, rounded HEAD ONLY, with big cheerful blue eyes, ivory eye whites and the same tiny closed friendly smile. Each head fills about 85% of its square cell, with clean transparent padding. Remove the tiny trailing body segments behind these four heads: the separate orange circular sprites will supply the neck and body in the game. Keep the four head directions LEFT, UP, RIGHT, DOWN, in that exact order. Keep the existing tangerine orange/golden palette, gentle brown outlines and cute 2D cartoon style. Keep canvas square and all 4x4 cell boundaries aligned exactly; do not move sprites between cells. Keep the remaining 12 cells unchanged, including all three circular body sprites, red apple and other creatures. Real transparent background; no pink or red on the worm, no teeth, no added text, labels, shadows, background or grid.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine this ONE top-down orange worm head sprite, still facing RIGHT. Make the head shorter and rounder, with a large rounded rear and only a tiny blunt snout at the rightmost edge; overall silhouette nearly square (about 1.1 times as wide as tall), filling 85% of the square canvas. It should attach naturally to a round worm body on its LEFT. Keep the genuine overhead view, two blue eyes on top looking RIGHT, orange/gold palette, clean soft shading and brown outline. Keep the small eating-mouth notch on the RIGHTMOST OUTER TIP, never on the face toward the viewer. No camera-facing smile, emoji face, body segments, apple or other objects. Preserve actual alpha transparency, no text, shadow or background.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: overhead forest canopy texture for the connected solid walls of a top-down nature snake game. Landscape 4:3 image, 1280 by 960 pixels or 1448 by 1086. Fill the whole canvas with ONE unbroken dense woodland canopy, seen straight down from above. Many softly overlapping rounded oak crowns and small conifer clusters, broad leaves, deep forest green and muted teal, pockets of natural dark shade, restrained painterly cartoon detail with clear large forms readable on mobile. Tree crowns should be irregular sizes about one tenth of image width and overlap so there is no exposed ground anywhere. This image will be sampled continuously across neighbouring wall cells: NO grid, square patches, cell boundaries, margins, outlines around the image or individual tiles, rows of isolated tree icons, trunks seen from the side, paths, clearings, grass floor, flowers, characters, text, fruit, perspective, UI or single giant tree. All four canvas edges are filled with leaves that continue naturally beyond the frame. Rich but calm forest mass, warm daylight highlights, gentle depth, matching a friendly storybook garden game. This is a continuous top-down forest texture, not a tileset atlas. Actual final bitmap.

packing: tools/make_art.py packs overhead terrain and orange body cells, rotating head-profile.png to the four movement directions. Connected walls share a surface with outlines only on exposed edges. Forest walls sample one board-wide canopy; the portrait mirror is mechanically rotated, preserving every join.
